notes.title: Dev Update 2025-06-06
notes.notes: [p]Recently we have made a few changes primarily focusing on beginner players. First of all we have updated the tutorial in many different ways. We have reworked what information the tutorial teaches to the player and made some changes to how that information is presented with the goal of making the initial learning of the game smoother. But that is not the only change to the tutorial. We have also aimed to make the tutorial more interesting with more things to find and explore as well as making a complete visual rework to the tutorial. [/p][p]That being said we still have some work left, especially in connection to the tutorial boss encounters and cutscenes. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/6c6db66cdacc69845ab007707245c0a7adcc9217.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/a25f5fac2f16c654a18cfab0b8090db4fe1c4c85.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Another change that we have made is a rework of how the rainbow combo works. The core system of making a rainbow combo deals some extra damage and allows the player to get more paint, but it should now be clearer to the player how it works and therefore easier to do. We have also added some more visual effects to it and made some quality of life changes. As the rainbow combo is an important core mechanic for the game we have also given more opportunity to the player to learn the mechanic. [/p][p]Some more work that has been done the last couple of weeks is an improvement to UI controls and a continued work on adding localisation to more languages. This is however not implemented to closed beta as of now. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/32638f49c9679b1edb82088515fef553f2c6bd3e.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Go visit Sylvia's newly renovated home.[/p][p]MP Team[/p]

notes.title: Dev Update 2025-05-23
notes.notes:
These past two weeks we have introduced a new NPC into the caves of Painted Peril! We hope everyone will enjoy the presence of Tizo the traveling trinket trader! Err… or at least his cart for now… In Tizo's cart Sylvia can find many of her precious items which Tizo has collected on his journeys through the caves. And as a trinket trader Tizo would be more than happy to trade his trinkets with yours as you find each other in the caves. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/0a03298662fbb5c242f7b8ab44e2050c0289a39a.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/0bd65dcff978a08f5501e858d140152bbe20a423.jpg[/img]

Besides Tizo we have also had some major balance changes made to all spells in the game. Before spell power was calculated by “bottle power” + “color power”, this has now changed to “bottle power” x “color power”. This will help ensure stronger spells scale on a similar level as smaller spells that summon multiple projectiles but with lower power. We have also had a rebalance to yellow color to ensure that lower power spells feel overall more satisfying to use. 

Lastly we have also tackled a bunch of bug fixes and generally improved the quality of life for Sylvia, as long as she doesn't run into any enemies. 
And, we almost forgot to tell you; we have also added eight new items into the game and reworked and rebalanced some existing items to make them more interesting and useful. Maybe you can find some of them in Tizo’s cart. 

Keep trading
MP Team

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/3c50c313e61c0a1ec392501422de809c695845c6.jpg[/img]

Tjena, during the last two weeks we have been busy with updating the level progression of the game. Meaning we have added and changed some routes of what level exit that leads to where to make the players decision on where to go more meaningful. An addition to this has been to rework the system of keys and locked doors by adding more locked regions and level exits as well as adding the potential to get more keys through the new Willow Crates that will spawn in the levels.

notes.title: Dev Update 2025-03-14
notes.notes:
During the last two weeks we have been hard working in doing some major reworks of the core color system. Therefore, to start off we thought it would be interesting to discuss some of the underlying issues with the previous system which lead to making the reworks. 
First of all the game is a mechanically complicated game that requires new players to learn a lot in the beginning to be able to play the game at all. This often overwhelmed new players which understandably caused frustration. The second issue was that many of the mechanics felt clunky in practice, even though they could be interesting in theory. This was especially true in how the player casts spells and needs to pick up colors from enemies. The third issue is that the game is currently too difficult, especially in the beginning. The difficulty comes both from the scaling and placement of enemies but also from the core mechanics itself. It is hard to think about color theory, battle enemies, and keep track of the amount of paint you have all at the same time. 

To address these issues we broke down the rework of the core color system to three main fixes. First of all we have added the ability to cast spells with empty bottles. These colorless spells only deal a bit of damage and do not have any other effects that the colors have. This makes it less punishing when a bottle runs out of color and it allows us to simplify the start of the tutorial by only introducing bottles first. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/f08d788c058d9d1bac2b554808772719b4ddd3a1.jpg[/img]

The second major change we have made is to completely remove the ability to pick up color from enemies. Instead we have added a few color shrines in each level where the player can pick up color. In addition to this we have significantly increased both the maximum capacity of bottles and how much paint you get when picking up colors. This separates the color pickup decision from combat itself, which gives more time when making the decision of what colors to use. This also allows us to introduce colors even slower to the player, meaning that the player doesn’t need to learn all colors at the same time and can instead introduce them one at a time. Increasing the amount of color the player has does also increase the time in between when the player needs to pick up more color. This change is something that we are currently testing, meaning that it is not out on the closed beta yet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/7fdb0fcef30a9960920f3727cd5774bcc55a711d.png[/img]

The third fix that we will start working on next week is a rework to the color combat controls to make them less clunky. We will update you more on this in the future. In addition to these three main fixes to the color combat system we will also look more into updating the tutorial and making level and enemy balances to address the final underlying issues we are currently tackling. 
But that is all for this time.

Test and learn!
MP Team

notes.title: Dev Update 2024-10-25
notes.notes:
Another Friday, another weekly update! So what has happened since last time? Well to begin with we have continued working on some spells, this week we added the Elemental Slime to the closed beta. We have also, as expected, made some tweaks to the spells added last week to balance them further, more spells are also coming.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/a81bf8592b69a8ee939f9d5c0df98ccc341d9fd7.png[/img]

One of the larger changes we have made to the gameplay feel of the game is reworking the red color effect. We found the earlier version of this effect problematic, because the dynamic of giving almost complete control of healing distribution to the player made it difficult to balance the game and players were also way too dependent on needing to have red in at least one bottle. To add insult to injury, using the red color often felt a bit off. The most efficient way of using the color was often to just find an enemy on its own and then spamming the color for a bit until full health was reached. Not great game design. 
To address these issues we removed the red color to heal the player, and instead added a mechanic of temporary health. Hopefully this will make players less reliant on red in general while still allowing for making some specific builds around using red.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/36f34b524497dffd57f14e23dfcfde138c4ef15b.png[/img]

At last we have also been working on changing the item distribution and in-game economic balance. Our goal here is to balance things out and while still keeping some levels of exciting 
randomness. These changes are still a work in progress and will be live on the closed beta soon-ish.

Be REDy.
E&M

notes.title: Dev Update 2024-10-04
notes.notes:
Oh boy, this week has been intense. This week we have been busy with attending several events during the Finnish Game Week, mainly the IGDA Leadership day, Pocket Gamer Connects Helsinki, and W Love Games. We have met several nice people, discussed game design with other industry students and professionals and seen several interesting games and game concepts. In short, it has been great.

We were also lucky to be able to exhibit Painted Peril during the PGC conference, resulting in several new members to our small community. We want to welcome you all! 
During the conference we managed to achieve second place in the Big Indie Pitch competition which we are also very proud of, as the competition was harsh with several other games that in our opinion were also great. 

So what happens next you might wonder. Well, now in October we will be participating in the Steam Next Fest. This means that a new demo for the game will be available! But, as always if you want to test the game before that you can as always sign up for a playtesting session, we pick a few people from there each week.
Well, now I need to go and get some sleep as I need to pay back some time to the slumber bank. 

Go pet a stone!

notes.title: Dev Update 2024-09-27
notes.notes:
This week we have mainly worked on preparations for the conference next week. But we have made some additions for the game nonetheless. First, we have once again updated the player camera, now the camera should give the player a better view of what is upcoming when climbing and falling. Because let's be honest, accidentally climbing into an enemy was never fun for anyone. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/4769b70778ca2de6a47ee9d4cfc30d05800501ac.jpg[/img]

We have also added an additional mini boss room that separates the easier levels from the harder ones, in addition to this we have also rebalanced several harder enemies to make them more of a challenge when you have a well built build. Another balance change made is that we have tweaked the in-game economy to reduce the amount of astral pigments (coins) the player has in the later stages of a run. That being said, a more robust economy and item spawning system will be coming in a couple of weeks. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/9e0c3991cbf97386711fd48eec40fbd35951014b.jpg[/img]

We have also prepared the game for conference by fixing several small and medium bugs, as well as made some general polishing of the game. Part of this has been to add all eligible Kickstarter backers to the credits. We have also added more images to the tutorial. But that’s all for this week. Next week's update will probably be a bit unique, maybe a summary of our intense week? Well, we will see then!

notes.title: Dev Update 2024-09-13
notes.notes:
To start off this week's dev update we are happy to announce that we are going to Pocket Gamer Connects Helsinki at the start of October. So if you for any reason are there then please come and see us at the indie expo area. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/3d937ff5189b70cf17c751c9c83994b08256266a.png[/img]

So for the development this week we have focused on a couple of different things; we have added save and load systems, we have reworked and rebalanced many colors, and the UI for the player in game has been significantly improved.
Regarding the Save and Load system we have added a new currency, Petrified Pigment,  that is saved both between runs and between play sessions. When you unlock a new spell bottle it is now saved. You now also do not need to replay the tutorial each time you reboot the game. However, this save and load system is limited. The game is still a roguelike game, meaning that we do not save any progress within a run. We also feel that it is important to mention that because this game is still in closed beta we 
might reset save files in future updates, this will however not happen after game release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/c549c3ac8c3ba41f5e27d3e7dc0aa9d93a6ed9b7.png[/img]

Colors have been reworked, specifically the green and orange color effects. It was in both our opinion, and the opinion of many playtesters that these two colors were rather boring to use because they were not that interesting and to use them effectively it forced the player to wait. Orange color is now a lot more fast burning, with high damage up front but it fades away quickly. To make it more interesting it now also increases damage each time it spreads to a new enemy. 
Green color on the other hand deals very little poison damage at first, but to balance it poisoned enemies have significantly reduced attack damage. The twist with the green color is that each time a poisoned enemy dies the remaining poison jumps to an enemy nearby and doubles its poison damage. This encourages the player to focus poisoned enemies to kill poisoned enemies as fast to be able to spread the poison through as many enemies as possible before it runs out. Some general balance and smaller changes have also been done to most other colors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/aeeda39981c2ce1d9cef4d539b3357928477bedb.png[/img]

The final change done this week is that we have changed the players GUI, of note is that the players bottle placement has been moved to the bottom center of the screen and their placement layout has changed. This rearrangement was done to make it easier for players to notice what color they currently have selected and how to change the bottle. Of note is that we are still testing this new layout, so therefore this is your weekly reminder that our playtesters are the best.

Visit us at PGC!
E&M

notes.title: Dev Update 2024-09-06
notes.notes:
This week we have put a lot of effort into enemy and level variation. To start off we have added four completely new enemies that adds to the diversity of different encounters. This includes both very simple enemies and enemies with more complex attack patterns. In addition to the enemies implemented this week we also have several enemies in production.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/bde497191bc20f95a9ff7841fbe9eebebb15c421.jpg[/img]

So for the levels our aim this week has been to make each level feel more unique and interesting, while keeping the levels procedurally generated to make them slightly different each run. Of course adding more enemies and making some enemies unique to some levels does create a more unique feeling for that level, but for us that was not enough. Therefore we decided to update our generation algorithm once again to be able to design features unique to each level. To be able to make more interesting rooms we have also added platforms and bridges that the player can jump through and we have also added more decorations to some levels. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/1555f055fbb22e5d048d8e1107b0935dec6cb536.jpg[/img]

Other than that we have also rebalanced the color economy and level timers as they were a bit unbalanced since the changes last week. This was something that was also brought up in several playtests,  so we want to thank them for their feedback (as well as doing our weekly reminder that we are always looking for more playtesters, so if you are interested feel free to apply for a testing session in the questionnaire below). We have also been working on backer design rewards, so for you who have been participating in that we want to say that it has been really fun to hear your ideas and see your designs!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/85eeb69b22fa0a9ef8d0fdfd343748b66b4718bd.png[/img]

Go explore, and beware of the Crystal Crawlers!

notes.title: Dev Update 2024-08-30
notes.notes:
For this week we have made several updates to how the core color collection system works. For a starter the player can now hold down the pick up color button to remove the color from that bottle. The color is not however completely removed, instead it first tries to fill some of the other bottles if it is possible to fill them without mixing to a new color. This does not only 
give the player a tool to remove unwanted color, but it also allows for splitting color mixes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/b08061d6a2a04a0933d685e48efd1445b1d0f1ed.jpg[/img]

Another change made to color collection is that enemies now drop color on death and they take reduced damage when they are uncolored. This change was made to reduce the efficiency of repeatedly casting a spell and then picking up the color again. Another change that was made to the color collection system is that collecting color using the brush is now a bit smarter to reduce the instances where the player accidentally mixes colors when they do not want to do that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/2d5585a0f6f5ae167db944da4626892e2527cb7b.jpg[/img]

Some enemies have also been reworked and have had bug fixes. Spikey can no longer get stuck on the player when falling, the crystal bombarder is now a bit less oppressive and the Crystal Quake has got an additional completely new attack. Finally we have also reworked the timer and the consequences of running out of time. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44148302/91ea03aac3263cd22da224b3a0e9f82650e6dcec.jpg[/img]

For some general updates we have also decided to start posting these dev updates on the Steam page, YouTube and Instagram, in addition to the Kickstarter and Discord server. And as if you want to test the game by yourself then please sign up to a testing session using the questionnaire below. 

Collect and Forget
